title: Stabilize priming oscillation causing first-token latency and tokens/sec sag across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Customers experienced transient but repeated spikes in initial-token latency and a drop in sustained tokens/sec after a staged rollout of kernel scheduler v2.3.4 combined with a KV prefetch reordering. Affects hosted API, Dedicated GPU pools, and Private VPC deployments with heterogenous model mixes.
description: Observed behavior: starting 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC we began receiving customer escalations for elevated first-token latency (P95 up to 2.6x) and sustained tokens/sec reductions (~20-40%) across several workloads. Issue appears shortly after deployment of kernel scheduler v2.3.4 and the new KV prefetch ordering heuristic. Symptoms span hosted endpoints, dedicated pools, and private installs — not limited to a single region or model family. Hypothesis: the scheduler change induced oscillation in warmstart/hedged warm-up behavior for multi-tenant pools; combined with a prefetch ordering change this causes excessive KV cache churn for long-context requests, inflating priming cost and causing downstream throughput collapse. Priority is stabilizing customer-facing latency and throughput and preventing recurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Send a mix of short (20-60 token) and long (1k+ token) priming requests to a multi-tenant pool with model variants (fp16 and int8).
2) Observe first-byte/first-token and sustained tokens/sec over a 30 minute rolling window; compare to baseline trace prior to 2026-03-09
3) Toggle kernel scheduler between v2.3.3 and v2.3.4 in a replicated testbed, with and without new KV prefetch ordering enabled, to reproduce oscillation in warm-start frequency.
4) Verify that disabling KV reordering removes the priming oscillation while leaving the scheduler at v2.3.4 (narrow down interaction).
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: 08:15 UTC - Incident intake: CS flagged 5 customers, SRE paging. Triage owned by runtime infra; ticket created.
2026-03-10: 10:40 UTC - Initial triage: correlated regressions with kernel scheduler v2.3.4 rollouts. Replicated a small P95 first-token increase in staging with synthetic replay.
2026-03-10: 14:20 UTC - Experiment: disabled KV prefetch reordering in staging; observed immediate reduction in priming variance. Opened ENG-616162 for deeper KV prefetch investigation.

2026-03-11: 02:30 UTC - Mitigation: applied targeted routing policy that diverted traffic from high-variance multiplexer pools to stable low-latency variants for affected customers. Notified CS and customers A/B.

2026-03-12: 05:00 UTC - Interim rollback: rolled back scheduler change in two host pools experiencing highest impact (us-west-2 and eu-central-1). First-token latency returned to baseline in those pools within ~8 minutes.
2026-03-13: 12:00 UTC - Soft restart: performed soft weight-streamer restart across remaining affected Dedicated pools; observed 70% throughput recovery for most customer workloads.

2026-03-14: 16:45 UTC - Canary: deployed a patched scheduler candidate (v2.3.4-p1) with conservative warmstart heuristics to a canary ring; no regression observed over 24 hours. Preparing controlled rollout plan.
2026-03-15: 09:00 UTC - Ongoing: working on KV prefetch heuristics and adding metrics for priming churn; preparing postmortem and customer communications.
decisions: Rollback kernel scheduler v2.3.4 in affected pools as primary immediate mitigation
Throttle aggressive KV prefetch reordering until heuristics are improved
Implement per-pool hedged-warmstart cooldown to avoid oscillation under mixed request patterns
Add circuit-breaker to route traffic to latency-optimized model variants when priming variance exceeds threshold
acceptance_criteria: P95 first-token latency for affected endpoints within 10% of pre-2026-03-09 baseline for 48h
Sustained tokens/sec recovered to >= 98% of baseline across Dedicated pools for 24h
Patched scheduler candidate validated in canary and runbook updated with rollback/mitigation steps
Postmortem published and CS notifications sent to impacted customers
postmortem_plan: Collect detailed traces and KV cache metrics for three representative customers (hosted, dedicated, private)
Quantify correlation between warmstart frequency and model variant mix
Root-cause write-up with timeline and a proposal for a scheduler algorithm change that considers priming cost
Publish a blameless postmortem within 7 days and schedule knowledge-share with SRE/serving/runtime teams
notes_for_support: Use routing policy 'latency-protect' to divert traffic for high-sensitivity customers until patch is live
If customer reports recurrence after patched rollout, collect request id and pool id and attach 'priming-osc-2026' tag
CS template: explain immediate rollback and that we will perform a phased safe rollout after additional testing
